header: I made the filter box above a list of people understand DESIGNATIONS. These are pure functions, no database, no React.
* case does not matter and the dot after a short form is optional: gm, GM, Dy, dy. Asst, asst. Sr, Jr, Mgr, Mngr

* the initials of a designation mean THAT designation and no other: gm = General Manager, dgm = Dy. General Manager, agm = Asst. General Manager, cgm = Chief General Manager, ed = Executive Director, dic = Director In-charge, jo = Junior Officer (the first 18 months of a promotee; there may be none now), mo = Medical Officer

* a whole title is recognised the same way: "general manager" shows the General Managers only (not the Dy. or Asst. ones), "Dy. general manager", "asst. general manager", "sr mgr", "dy mngr", "jr mngr" ...
* "Asst.General Manager" (no space, as it may be stored) and "Asst. General Manager" are the same thing: dots and spaces never matter
* several designations in one box, separated by a comma (or ; | or the word "or"): gm, dgm, agm
* a designation can be combined with a word: "roy gm" (the General Managers named Roy)
* I read which titles exist from the list itself, so nothing here has to be kept up to date; a title that is not in the list shows no rows

* the ORIGIN of an executive, which I read from the ticket: an executive ticket is 4 + a second digit + four more digits, and the second digit never changes in a whole service life: 9 = joined directly as an executive (a direct recruit: a Management Trainee, MT, for the whole training, then Asst. Manager); any other digit = promoted from the non-executives (a promotee: called JO for the first 18 months, then holding the normal designation, a DGM or AGM later). "promotee", "promotees", "promoty", "promoted officers" show the promotees whatever their designation is today; "mt", "mts", "management trainee(s)", "direct", "direct recruit" the direct recruits. They combine with a designation or a word ("promotee agm", "direct gm", "promotee roy"). They work when the list shows a ticket column (otherwise they are plain text). "jo" is NOT one of these words: it is a designation (above), found by its title like any other.
Anything that is not a designation or an origin (a name, a ticket, a department, a code) I find as before, as text anywhere in the row.

symbols.name: squash
doc: I keep letters and digits only, so "Asst.General" and "Asst. General" both become "asstgeneral".

symbols.name: SHORT_WORDS
symbols.sig: const SHORT_WORDS: Record<string, string[]> = { asst: ["assistant"], dy: ["deputy"], sr: ["senior"], jr: ["junior"], mgr: ["manager"], mngr: ["manager"], …
doc: Short forms of one word; I ignore dots, so the dot after them is optional.

symbols.name: INITIALS
symbols.sig: const INITIALS: Record<string, string[]> = { dic: ["director", "in", "charge"], ed: ["executive", "director"], cgm: ["chief", "general", "manager"], gm: [" …
doc: Initials of a whole designation; each one means that designation and no other.

symbols.name: SHORT_ALONE
doc: A short form that already names a designation on its own ("Mgr" is the Manager).

symbols.name: canonicalTitle
doc: Gives the designation in one fixed spelling: "Asst.General Manager", "Asst. General Manager" and "Assistant General Manager" all give "assistant general manager".

symbols.name: isDesignationColumn
symbols.sig: const isDesignationColumn = (c: { key: string; label: string; kind: string }): boolean =>

params.name: c
params.type: { key: string; label: string; kind: string }

doc: Returns true only for the column that holds the designation of a person (not its code, grade or rank).

symbols.name: tidyDesignation
doc: I show a designation with a space after the dot ("Asst.General Manager" reads "Asst. General Manager"); the stored value is never changed.

symbols.name: splitAlternatives
doc: I treat "gm, dgm, agm" as three alternatives; a row that fits any one of them is shown.

symbols.name: Origin
doc: Where an executive came from, as I read it from the ticket: "promotee" (promoted from the non-executives), "direct" (joined directly as an executive: an MT, a Management Trainee) or "" (no executive ticket).

symbols.name: originOfTicket
doc: I read 49xxxx as a direct recruit and 40xxxx to 48xxxx as a promotee; anything else (a non-executive ticket, a blank, a code) gives no origin.

symbols.name: isTicketColumn
symbols.sig: const isTicketColumn = (c: { key: string; label: string; kind: string }): boolean =>

params.name: c
params.type: { key: string; label: string; kind: string }

doc: True for the column I take to hold the ticket number.

symbols.name: ORIGIN_PHRASES
doc: The words that ask for an origin (dots, dashes and capitals do not matter: "MT", "mts", "Promotee Officers"; "M.T." is two initials, a name search, not this). MT is the official term (my ruling, 30 Oct 2026).

members.name: title
doc: Holds the designation this alternative asks for (in canonical spelling), or null when it asks for none.

members.name: origin
doc: Holds the origin this alternative asks for ("" when none).

members.name: rest
doc: The remaining words; I require each one to be found, as text, somewhere in the row.

symbols.name: Enabled
doc: What the list can answer: designations need a designation column, origins need a ticket column. Without one, I treat the words as plain text.

symbols.name: takeSpan
symbols.sig: function takeSpan<T>(tokens: string[], pick: (words: string[], len: number) => T | null): { value: T; rest: string[] } | null
doc: I take the longest run of the alternative's words that `pick` accepts; the other words are what is left.

symbols.name: compileAlternative
symbols.sig: export function compileAlternative(alt: string, known: Set<string>, enabled: Enabled = { designations: true, origins: true }): CompiledAlternative
doc: I find the origin and the designation inside one alternative and leave the other words as plain text to find.

symbols.name: alternativeMatches
symbols.sig: export function alternativeMatches(c: CompiledAlternative, p: PreparedRow): boolean
